title: 128 numbers, one per neuron, make Gemma talk like a person
subtitle: Goal: casual replies like a person texting a friend, from a system prompt distilled into the model. The edit is one trained gain on each of 128 neurons: 128 numbers, written into the weights.
footnote: Example: the first test message, greedy reply (… = cut); tag = the judge's score for that reply. Bars: an LLM judge rates how much a reply reads like a real person texting a friend (1-5), mean over 60 test messages × 3 replies, thin line = 95% interval; random neurons: 3 sets trained the same way (range). A different recipe from the other demos: one gain per neuron, trained with a preservation loss.
caption: The edit scales 128 MLP neurons by trained gains (a -> a(1+g)), chosen by attribution and trained with a KL preservation loss on task replies. Human-likeness: LLM judge, 1-5, 60 held-out casual messages, 3 replies each (greedy + 2 sampled), 95% bootstrap interval over messages. Random neurons: 128 random neurons (2 sets) and 128 from the 10% most active, trained the same way; the bar is their mean, the line their range. Side effects from the demo's side-effects table.
